paper_title: Stochastic fluctuations of bosonic dark matter
coupling_convention: log10 g_aNN plotted; emitted as absolute g_aNN in GeV^-1
notes: This paper is a methodological/reinterpretation study showing that constraints on bosonic dark matter couplings derived in the T<<tau_c regime were overestimated by factors of ~3-10 due to neglecting the stochastic (Rayleigh-distributed) nature of the VULF amplitude. It does NOT present a new original exclusion limit; instead it applies correction factors to previously published constraints (CASPEr-ZULF, nEDM, dilaton searches). The exclusion plots (Figs. 3, 4) are rescaled versions of prior experiments' limits rather than new measurements, and no numerical limit tables/curves are provided in extractable form. Assumed local DM density rho_DM ~ 0.4 GeV/cm^3 is mentioned. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 3 shows stochastic (green) vs deterministic (gray) axion-nucleon g_aNN constraints. I traced the green (stochastic) lower boundary as it is this paper's primary result. Note: y-axis units are GeV^-1 which is unusual for a dimensionless g_aNN (canonical g_aNN is dimensionless); the paper plots g_aNN in GeV^-1 (derivative coupling normalization). Values emitted as plotted (absolute g_aNN in GeV^-1). The gap between ~1e-17 and 1e-16 eV corresponds to region not constrained.
